extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX authors submitting source to Evan Chen (math students, olympiad writers, mathematicians)
extracted.subtask_description: A LaTeX source style guide specifying required conventions and typesetting rules for mathematical documents submitted to Evan Chen. Covers source-line formatting, math typesetting, spacing, environments, and other coding/typographic conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of MUST/SHOULD keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: The keywords “MUST”, “MUST NOT”, “REQUIRED”, “SHALL”, “SHALL NOT”, “SHOULD”, “SHOULD NOT”, “RECOMMENDED”, “MAY”, and “OPTIONAL” are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the RFC2119 semantics when the document uses these capitalized terms so readers know the strength of each requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source line length and wrapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Source lines MUST be wrapped to be at most 100 characters long, except when impossible, and SHOULD be wrapped to at most 80 characters long.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert line breaks in natural places (end of sentences, after commas, between phrases/clauses). Short lines are acceptable if they improve legibility; you are not expected to fill the maximum width. Long URL-like exceptions permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation marks input
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation marks MUST be inputted correctly in LaTeX; you MUST NOT type a literal double-quote character (").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proper LaTeX input (e.g., `` and '') rather than raw " characters so typographic quotes render correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math operator commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators like \sin MUST be typeset correctly, either using builtin commands or using the \operatorname command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not write operator names as ordinary text inside math; use established macros (\sin, \log, etc.) or \operatorname{...} for custom operators to ensure correct spacing and styling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipses usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Ellipses MUST be written with amsmath’s \dots (or the appropriate AMSMath semantic dots \dotsc, \dotso, \dotsb, \dotsi, \dotsm where required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use older commands \ldots or \cdots. Use semantic ellipses when auto-detection would pick the wrong type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammatical punctuation placement relative to inline math
rubrics_metrics.description: Grammatical commas and grammatical periods MUST NOT appear in inline math.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punctuation that belongs to the surrounding sentence should be outside the math delimiters. Examples: 'Thus $x=3$.' (not 'Thus $x=3.$') and 'Let $x_1$, \dots, $x_n$ be integers' (not 'Let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be integers'). Mathematical commas used inside expressions like f(a,b) remain inside math mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extraneous spaces before punctuation or around dollar signs
rubrics_metrics.description: There MUST NOT be extraneous spaces preceding punctuation or around dollar signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid spaces like '$x $ ,' or ' $ x$'; punctuation and math delimiters should not be separated by stray spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two spaces after sentences optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Using two spaces after a sentence is OPTIONAL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is allowed but not required; follow other readability conventions instead of enforcing two spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing around binary operators
rubrics_metrics.description: There SHOULD generally be spaces around binary operators and relations such as + or =, but these spaces MAY be omitted for short expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spacing MUST be symmetric (e.g., '$x = 3$' acceptable, '$x =3$' is not). Use consistent spacing for readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delimiter sizing and balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Delimiters of complex expressions SHOULD be balanced with \left and \right, or variants of \big.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scalable delimiters to match expression height rather than fixed-size symbols for readability and correct typesetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not approximate predefined operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximations of predefined operators MUST NOT be used (e.g., '||' MUST NOT be used in place of \parallel, '.' in place of \cdot, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the proper LaTeX symbols and macros for standard operators to guarantee correct spacing and semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display math delimiters
rubrics_metrics.description: For single-line display math, double dollar signs MUST NOT ever be used; use \[ ... \] instead (REQUIRED).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-dollar syntax is deprecated and causes spacing issues; prefer \[ ... \].

rubrics_metrics.name: Line breaks around display delimiters
rubrics_metrics.description: Inserting line breaks after \[ and before \] is OPTIONAL; if the line break is not included there MUST be a space instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either put \[ on its own line or ensure a space follows it; similarly for the closing \]. This avoids token-joining issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line breaks before/after displayed expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: There SHOULD be a single line break before and after displayed expressions; there MUST NOT be double line breaks unless the displayed line is intentionally its own paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inserting extra blank lines around displays except when you mean to start a new paragraph (which is rarely the case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid adjacent single-line displays for multi-equation sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: When a series of equations are too long to fit on a single line, one MUST NOT have adjacent \[ ... \] expressions; in most cases, the align* environment SHOULD be used instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use align* for multi-line equation groups instead of stacking multiple single-line displays; this preserves alignment and spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: align* environment placement
rubrics_metrics.description: When using align*, the \begin{align*} and \end{align*} invocations MUST be on their own line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the environment delimiters alone on a line for readability and consistent source formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line breaks after \\ in displays
rubrics_metrics.description: There MUST be a line break after each \\ invocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There MAY be additional line breaks for legibility, and there MUST be additional line breaks if necessary to keep line length within the specified limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation inside environments
rubrics_metrics.description: The contents of any \begin{...} ... \end{...} environment SHOULD be indented by at least two spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent indentation (minimum two spaces) for readability of nested environments and blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: No trailing whitespace
rubrics_metrics.description: There MUST NOT be any trailing whitespace; no line may end with a whitespace character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure editors are configured to strip trailing spaces to avoid spurious diffs and formatting issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph breaks formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph breaks MUST be typeset using two or more line breaks (one empty line between paragraphs) and MUST NOT be typeset using \\\\ or other similar antics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the standard blank-line method to separate paragraphs in source; do not fake paragraphs with forced line breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variables and constants in math mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Any mathematical variables MUST be enclosed in dollar signs; this also includes constants like 1 when used in a mathematical context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: write 'let $n=2022$' and 'add $1$ to both sides' instead of leaving numbers or variables outside math mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function domain/range colon
rubrics_metrics.description: When specifying domains and ranges of mathematical functions, one MUST use \colon instead of a plain colon ':', e.g. $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \colon to get proper spacing and semantics in function type expressions.
